items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-06-20
items.q: Justin, Adam, and Emma, we'd go right into things.

ctx.x: Well, getting back, did you ever think of yourself as a rock and roll star? As a rock and roll artist? Yeah, yeah. You did?

Typical, I was a rock and roll artist. See, When I Meet My Girl was defined as the first rockabilly tune to be the hit. You know, because it was a national record. And it was the first rockabilly. And from there, you know, I was strictly rock and roll. See, I played all of the white colleges. What could we talk about? I played from here, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Alabama. I played all of them. And it was strictly, you know, rock and roll. We did some of the, like, What I Say, Oop-Oop-A-Doo, was the tunes. But,…
Well, when we were on that, I have a note here about, how did you all travel when you were on the road? How did you, in those days?
